text:
sanjay: quick heads-up — I ran a head-to-head replay vs synthetic bench focused on kernel selection, batching heuristics, and KV cache behavior across eu-west-1 and us-east-1. summary below, logs linked.

deploy-bot: loadtest started (id: lb-rt-1851304823). config: replay=live-traffic-2025-11, synth=seqdist-v2.yaml (p95_len=256, p50_len=64), rate=450rps/region, duration=8m, kv_priming=on for replay, off for synth initially.

lee: raw numbers (rounded):
  - replay auto-kernel (eu): p50=24ms p95=82ms p99=230ms tps=410
  - synth auto-kernel (eu): p50=20ms p95=74ms p99=215ms tps=430
  - replay auto-kernel (us): p95=86ms p99=260ms tps=395
  - synth auto-kernel (us): p95=78ms p99=238ms tps=415

zoe: noted: replay p95 consistently higher. what were kv hit rates for those runs?

maria: kv hit-rate: replay eu ~0.72, synth eu ~0.15 (cold). us-east similar: replay 0.68, synth 0.12. after a 10m prewarm for synth, synth p95 converged to replay within ~2-3%.

sanjay: kernel selection notes: with policy=auto the selector prefers `fused-attn-v2` for seq_len>=256, falls back to `aten-attn` otherwise. observed kernel_switch_count spikes when KV hit-rate changes — likely because cached KV alignment + kernel memory layout mismatch causes us to reselect kernels mid-session. kernel switch penalty ~6-8ms on average.

lee: profiler snippet (from eu replay run):
```
kernel_select: fused-attn-v2 (seq=512) 45%, aten-attn (seq<=128) 40%, fallback-ref 15%
kernel_switch_cost_ms: mean=7.3 med=6.1 p95=12.8
batching_util: avg_batch=10 target_latency=75ms
kv_cache: hit_rate=0.72 miss_cost_ms=3.6
```

zoe: we also saw more kernel thrash during the region-drain failover simulation. when we triggered drain in eu, traffic moved to us and the fallback model variant (quantized-small) in us caused higher CPU-bound time and increased p99 by ~7-10%.

maria: regression note: compared to baseline from last week, us-east p99 is +3% even without failover. root cause trace points to extra serialization in routing-proxy v2 (commit a1b2c3) that affects request fanout during high-concurrency bursts.

sanjay: reproduce steps I used: 1) run replay harness with kv_priming on for 10m prewarm, 2) run synth harness with identical seq distribution and same RNG seed for sampling, 3) toggle kernel policy: auto vs force-fused vs force-no-switch, 4) run a drain at t+3m to exercise failover, 5) collect kernel_switch_count, kv_hits, p95/p99, per-model cpu/gpu util.

lee: question — can we get a like-for-like comparison if synth was cold? probably not useful. we should standardize on: run a 10m steady prewarm phase, then measurement window 5m, and record priming state. also include a run forcing kernel policy `no-switch` to measure the cost of switches themselves.

maria: queued a forced no-switch job: id rt-1851-no-switch scheduled at 1851304920. will run across both regions.

perfbot: job rt-1851-no-switch started at 1851304920.

perfbot: intermediate summary (t+2m):
  - no-switch eu p95=80ms p99=225ms (vs auto p95=82ms)
  - kernel_switch_count dropped from avg 4.2 -> 0.3 per-connection
  - kv_hit unchanged (prewarm done)

zoe: so kernel switches are a measurable source of tail latency. when combined with KV miss storms during failover, we see compounding effects.

sanjay: behavioral root cause hypothesis: during failover, traffic mix changes (short vs long sequences), cache warmness drops for many shards, selector oscillates between kernels as it reacts to instantaneous seq distribution, and that oscillation creates extra CPU/GPU setup cost and occasional blocking on the memcopy paths.

lee: actionable items proposed:
  1) add `kernel_switch_count` and `kernel_switch_latency_ms` to the replay harness output (per-request).
  2) add a `staggered-failover` option in the routing test to gradually shift traffic (5s ramps) to reduce KV miss storms.
  3) baseline tests must include KV prewarm for 10m, and a cold-run variant for completeness.
  4) short-term mitigation: default kernel policy -> `prefer-stable` (bias against switching unless p90 latency improvement > 10%).

maria: I'll open a PR with the harness changes and a routing-proxy rollback candidate for the serialization regression. linking to draft: https://go/repo/rt/harness/1851 (internal).

zoe: +1 on prefer-stable. but we should quantify cost vs quality: add eval-run with a held-out prompt set to check output parity when kernel forced.

lee: also we need an apples-vs-oranges check (ha) — make sure model variant fallback counts are recorded so we can normalize p99 by fallback fraction.

sanjay: can we annotate the run metadata with `fallback_fraction`, `kv_prewarm_seconds`, `kernel_policy`, `seq_seed` — so future comparisons are deterministic?

maria: yes will add those fields to the job metadata schema.

perfbot: job rt-1851-no-switch finished. final artifacts uploaded: s3://ci-perf/rt/1851304823/rt-1851-no-switch/{metrics,profiles,logs}.

lee: next step: mari a, can you run staggered-failover with prefer-stable ON and forced prewarm for synth so we get a clean comparison replay vs synth under the new routing? schedule?

maria: scheduling staggered-failover at 1851305020 (10m). will post results.

zoe: thanks team. this run gives us a clear signal to prioritize prefer-stable and an improved routing failover ramp. small docs note: add methodology block to perf playbook (prewarm, identical seq dist, RNG seed, record kernel switch metrics, record fallback fraction). :memo: 

sanjay: perfect. after maria's staggered run, let's reconvene and decide whether to ship prefer-stable as default for the next canary. :thumbsup:

lee: ack.

maria: ack.
